record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: Does intermittency in multiparticle final states have a direct connection with fundamental perturbative QCD, given that perturbative calculations predict intermittent behavior for emitted gluons but hadronization may change the strength of the effect observed for hadrons?

evidence.quote: At a deeper level, it is a basic problem to see whether the intermittency effect has some connection with the fundamental theory at all!

Interesting developments have been reported at the conference [12,19], showing from three different calculations that perturbative QCD, within some approximation framework, is intermittent in the strict sense for emitted gluons (in the axial gauge). However, hadronization effects may be important, since the predicted behaviour for gluons is similar in form but different in strength from that observed for hadrons[19].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider high-energy multiparticle production processes, in which the final state consists of many hadrons distributed in phase space. For a phase-space variable (such as rapidity), divide an interval of size $\Delta$ into $M$ equal bins of size $\delta = \Delta/M$ and, for each event, let $n_m$ denote the multiplicity in bin $m$. The normalized factorial moments of order $q \ge 2$ are defined by
$$F_q(\delta) = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M} \frac{\langle n_m(n_m-1)\cdots(n_m-q+1)\rangle}{\langle n_m\rangle^q},$$
where $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes the event average. The system is said to exhibit intermittency if, as $\delta \to 0$, $F_q(\delta)$ grows as a power law $F_q(\delta) \propto \delta^{-\phi_q}$ with strictly positive intermittency exponents $\phi_q > 0$.

Within perturbative QCD (for instance, in the axial gauge using the double-leading-log or modified leading-log approximation for parton cascades), factorial moments of the emitted gluon multiplicity distribution in small angular or rapidity windows can be computed and are known to display intermittent behavior of the form above, with calculable exponents $\phi_q^{\text{parton}}$. Hadronization (the non-perturbative transition from partons to hadrons) is expected to modify these exponents, so that the measured hadronic exponents $\phi_q^{\text{hadron}}$ may differ in magnitude (though not necessarily in qualitative form) from $\phi_q^{\text{parton}}$.

Question: Does the intermittency phenomenon observed in hadronic multiparticle final states admit a direct, quantitative derivation from perturbative QCD? More precisely, is there a controlled theoretical framework — incorporating both perturbative parton branching and a model of hadronization (e.g., local parton–hadron duality or a definite fragmentation scheme) — that reproduces the experimentally measured intermittency exponents $\phi_q^{\text{hadron}}$ for all $q \ge 2$ in high-energy hadronic, leptonic, and nuclear collisions, and that explains why the strength of the effect differs between gluon-level and hadron-level distributions?
artifact.status_search_result: Web sources confirm that intermittency in multiparticle final states is widely interpreted as a consequence of QCD parton cascading, with local parton–hadron duality (LPHD) used to connect parton- and hadron-level distributions. Perturbative QCD calculations reproduce the qualitative form of intermittency for gluons, but a complete, quantitatively predictive derivation of the measured hadronic intermittency exponents from first-principles QCD (including a controlled treatment of hadronization) does not appear to be established. The status of the precise question remains unclear from the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Hadron multiplicities — Physics Reports
status_evidence.snippet: Intermittency observed in all types of hadronic collisions; jet-cascading is the most likely interpretation; LPHD relates partons and hadrons.
status_evidence.claim: Intermittency is linked to perturbative QCD cascading via LPHD, but quantitative agreement with hadronic data requires non-perturbative input.

status_evidence.title: Multiparticle production and perturbative QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Perturbative QCD describes main features of multiparticle production; intermittency and fractality are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: Perturbative QCD captures qualitative features of intermittency, but the strength of the effect at hadron level remains influenced by hadronization.

status_evidence.title: Intermittency in multiparticle production at high energy
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational treatment of intermittency in multiparticle final states.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes intermittency as a robust empirical phenomenon whose origin in fundamental QCD remains under investigation.
